proposal.name: flatten-garment
proposal.purpose: Add an explicit coupled-bite test so a whole-garment slide is detected and stopped instead of being completed as if it were an opening pull.
proposal.guidance: Strengthen the structure-validation and continuation steps: treat local height relief alone as insufficient evidence of a free layer edge, and prefer anchors where a layer boundary is traceable as an outline in more than one view. During the first small lift, compare the grasped region against the rest of the footprint; if the untouched part of the garment moves with the grasp, treat the bite as coupled through layers, release or re-plan, and do not proceed to lateral motion. After the action, read a translation of the whole footprint with unchanged internal fold pattern, unchanged occlusion of printed regions, and unchanged standing folds as a coupled-bite outcome rather than a transport-distance shortfall, so the next attempt revises anchor and bite geometry instead of pull length. Also keep the final resting position inside all evaluation views so openness stays measurable.
proposal.rationale: The existing skill says to stop when a lift reveals no supported structure, but not how to recognise the specific coupled-bite signature seen here, which let a validated-expansion plan spend its whole pull budget dragging an unchanged bundle and misread the earlier shortfall as insufficient transport.
evidence: Camera A landmarks (collar with white label, left sleeve tip, green print block, pink square row) all shifted down-frame by a similar offset with unchanged relative geometry.
Print occlusion by the folded sleeve and diagonal roll is identical before and after in both views.
Camera B depth still shows the same standing crest with missing-depth speckle at its tip and the same shadow crevice beneath it.
The garment now clips the bottom edge of both Camera A and Camera B, leaving part of the outcome unmeasurable.
